key_insight: Temporal synchronization between video and music can be achieved by matching when and how much change occurs (temporal structure) rather than trying to map semantic content across modalities.
problem_solved: Existing text-to-music and cross-modal generators lack fine-grained temporal control and cannot produce music that is time-aligned to video events without paired training data; V2M-Zero enables zero-pair, time-aligned video-to-music generation.
method: Extract modality-agnostic temporal-change representations from video (motion/scene-change signals) and music (onset/intensity patterns).
Learn a zero-pair alignment that matches temporal change patterns across modalities, focusing on 'when' and 'how much' change rather than semantic correspondence.
Condition a music synthesis module with the aligned temporal-control signal to generate time-aligned audio for the input video.
impact: Provides a practical way to generate synchronized music for arbitrary videos without paired datasets, enabling scalable multimodal content creation and refined temporal control for audio-visual generation tasks.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing video events (frame thumbnails) aligned to generated music waveform/spectrogram peaks to illustrate temporal correspondence.
Schematic block diagram: video change extractor → temporal alignment module → music generator (highlight zero-pair training loop).
Before/after comparison: naive (semantic mismatch) vs. V2M-Zero (tight temporal sync) with short audio/video stills.
Icon set: clock/timeline (temporal), waveform (audio), eye/camera (video), and a 'zero' badge to denote zero-pair/zero-shot.
paper_authors: Yan-Bo Lin, Jonah Casebeer, Long Mai, Aniruddha Mahapatra, Gedas Bertasius
